t: Israel: Eisenkot poised to form the next government
s: Parties representing 67 lawmakers recommended Gadi Eisenkot to form the next government, against 46 for Benjamin Netanyahu. President Isaac Herzog was due to assign the mandate on Sunday, November 8.

t: Poland: six killed in a shooting in Kraków
s: A gunman opened fire on Saturday, November 7, in Kraków's main square, killing six people and wounding about fifteen before being shot and wounded by police. Authorities say he acted alone and held ultranationalist views.

t: United States: Democrats retake Congress
s: Democrats won control of both the House of Representatives and the Senate in the November 3 midterm elections, according to projections. Several seats were still to be called.

t: Pope Leo XIV arrives in Argentina
s: According to the schedule released by the Vatican, the pope leaves Uruguay for Argentina on November 8 (Buenos Aires, Córdoba, Luján) before ending his tour in Peru from November 11 to 17. No pope had visited Argentina since 1987.

t: EU leaders to meet in Dublin on November 13
s: An informal meeting of EU heads of state and government takes place in Dublin on November 13, the day after the European Political Community summit, held in the same city on November 12.

t: Wages: social conference on Monday at Matignon
s: Following the November 5 protests, Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu is meeting unions and employers on Monday, November 9. Labour Minister Jean-Pierre Farandou wants to lift the net minimum wage above €1,500 a month; the CFDT union is asking for an extra €100 net, the CGT for a 10% raise.

t: A wave of hoax bomb threats in European skies
s: At least twenty flights were targeted on Thursday, November 5, and all landed safely. In France, the Évreux prosecutor opened an investigation into the pilot of an Aer Lingus flight who allegedly refused to land at the Évreux military air base.

t: 2027 presidential race: LFI unveils Mélenchon's platform
s: La France insoumise presented the new version of Jean-Luc Mélenchon's platform on November 6 and 7, with a rally in Le Bourget. Ecology becomes its cornerstone.

t: Besançon: 13 arrests after a jewellery factory heist
s: Thirteen suspects were arrested after the armed robbery of a jewellery factory in Besançon, France's national anti-organised-crime prosecutor said on November 4.

t: Wall Street: the Nasdaq 100 has its worst day since 2020
s: On Thursday, November 5, the Nasdaq 100 fell 6.36%, the S&P 500 lost 4.35% and the Dow Jones dropped 1,833 points. Investors sold memory-chip, storage, chip-equipment and data-centre stocks.

t: US jobs: 165,000 added in October
s: The US economy added 165,000 jobs in October, far more than expected, and the unemployment rate stands at 4.1%, according to the Bureau of Labor Statistics.

t: Fed: a December rate hike looks increasingly likely
s: After the jobs report, CME's FedWatch tool put the probability of a quarter-point Federal Reserve rate hike in December at 76.8%.

t: OpenAI unveils GPT-6 Cyber, a vulnerability-hunting model
s: Restricted to vetted security teams, the model found 81 serious flaws in Firefox and produced 948 exploits for Linux kernel flaws, which were reported to maintainers, according to figures released by OpenAI.

t: FlashProve: proving which AI model produced an answer
s: Anthropic open-sourced FlashProve, a research prototype that cryptographically proves a response came from a given model without revealing its weights. The system remains costly and is not deployed in any product.

t: Dropbox buys Tigris Data for $350 million
s: Dropbox will acquire Tigris Data, a start-up specialising in storage for AI applications, for about $350 million in cash. The deal is expected to close in the fourth quarter.

t: Blight-resistant rice thanks to an AI-designed tool
s: University of Missouri researchers made rice plants resistant to bacterial blight, a disease that threatens harvests in Asia and Africa, using OpenCRISPR-1, an AI-designed, freely usable gene-editing tool. Published in the journal aBIOTECH, the work is at the lab stage: commercial varieties are several years away.

t: Measles: nearly 4,900 US cases this year
s: The CDC counted 4,852 measles cases as of October 29, 264 more than in its previous update. 96% of patients were unvaccinated or had an unknown vaccination status.

t: COP31 opens on Monday in Antalya
s: The UN climate conference runs from November 9 to 20 in Türkiye. Murat Kurum presides, and Australia's Chris Bowen leads the negotiations.

t: Champions League: Lens thrashed 9-1 by Como
s: On Wednesday, November 4 at Bollaert, Lens suffered the heaviest defeat ever for a French club in European competition. No team had ever conceded nine goals at home in the Champions League.

t: Israel: Eisenkot tasked with forming the government
s: President Isaac Herzog on Sunday gave Gadi Eisenkot the mandate to form the next government, after the October 27 election. He has 28 days, extendable by 14, and promises a “national emergency government”.

t: Ukraine: massive Russian strikes ahead of the Abu Dhabi talks
s: Volodymyr Zelensky accuses Russia of stepping up strikes on the power grid to gain leverage before the US-brokered negotiations in Abu Dhabi on Tuesday. Moscow launched 172 drones and 36 ballistic missiles, including North Korean-supplied KN-23s.

t: Pope Leo XIV welcomed to Argentina by Javier Milei
s: Arriving in Buenos Aires on Sunday, the pope called for democracy to be protected and said the economy must serve people, not the other way around, a veiled critique of Javier Milei's austerity policy according to the AP. He will then travel on to Peru.

t: Wages: social conference at Matignon today
s: Sébastien Lecornu is meeting the leaders of the main unions and employer organisations today on purchasing power and wages, following the November 5 protests. The minimum wage is at the heart of the talks: the CFDT union wants an extra €100 net.

t: Tokyo: the Nikkei drops almost 6% on Friday
s: The Tokyo Stock Exchange closed down 5.96% on Friday at 57,434.77 points, dragged down by technology stocks. The Topix lost 5.9%.

t: OpenAI raises $11 billion at a $1.25 trillion valuation
s: OpenAI has closed a first tranche of about $11 billion in a round that could reach $20 billion, at a $1.25 trillion valuation, according to Bloomberg. The company has not announced it officially.

t: COP31 opens in Antalya with lowered ambitions
s: The UN climate conference opens today in Antalya, Türkiye, and runs until November 20. According to Bloomberg, its agenda is narrower than at previous COPs and ambitions have been scaled back.

t: Route du Rhum: Tom Laperche wins in record time
s: Tom Laperche (SVR-Lazartigue) won the Route du Rhum in the Ultim class overnight from Saturday to Sunday, in 6 days, 13 hours and 27 minutes. He beat the record set by Charles Caudrelier in 2022 by more than six hours.

t: F1: Lando Norris wins the São Paulo Grand Prix
s: The McLaren driver won Sunday's race at Interlagos, ahead of Max Verstappen, who climbed from 21st place, and Isack Hadjar.

t: Ligue 1: Marseille win 2-1 at Lens
s: Marseille won on Sunday at Bollaert, four days after Lens's rout against Como. Amine Gouiri opened the scoring in the 2nd minute, Florian Thauvin equalised, and Keyliane Abdallah gave OM the win in the 82nd.

t: Kraków: the gunman dies in hospital
s: The gunman who killed six people and wounded fifteen on Saturday, November 7, in Kraków's main square died in hospital on Monday, according to police. He had been wounded by officers during the attack. Authorities describe a far-right-inspired attack.

t: Ukraine: Europeans join the Abu Dhabi talks
s: European officials are set to take part this week in the US-brokered talks between Russia and Ukraine in Abu Dhabi. The Kremlin objected, saying the negotiations are strictly trilateral.

t: Trump says his deportations were “too tough” after the midterms
s: In an interview aired on Sunday, November 8, Donald Trump said his deportation policy had been too tough and hurt him in the midterm elections. He said he was open to an immigration deal with Democrats.

t: Minimum wage to rise 1.6% from December 1
s: Following the social conference at Matignon on Monday, November 9, Sébastien Lecornu announced an early increase in the minimum wage (Smic), to €1,502 net a month on December 1. Unions say the rise is insufficient, and the CGT is calling a strike on November 17.

t: Paris stocks rebound as oil prices fall
s: The CAC 40 gained 1.16% on Monday, November 9, to 8,233.30 points, supported by falling crude prices. STMicroelectronics led the index with a 5.30% gain.

t: Nvidia falls after an investigation targeting CEO Jensen Huang
s: Nvidia shares fell about 4% on Monday, November 9. On Sunday, the board opened an independent investigation into Jensen Huang's relationship with an executive suspected by US intelligence of spying for China. The company says it has no reason to believe its secrets were compromised.

t: COP31: opening in Antalya amid a finance dispute
s: The UN climate conference opened on Monday, November 9, in Antalya. Rich and developing countries clashed from the outset over climate finance, delaying the adoption of the agenda.

t: WMO: 2015-2026, the twelve warmest years on record
s: In its update published for COP31, the World Meteorological Organization says 2015-2026 will be the warmest twelve-year period on record. The years 2023 to 2026 are the four warmest in the observational record.

t: Ligue 1: Lille win 2-1 at Rennes and climb to second
s: LOSC won 2-1 at Stade Rennais on Sunday, November 8, in the 10th round, and moved up to second place in the table.

t: Ligue 1: Brest beat Lyon 2-0
s: Stade Brestois beat Olympique Lyonnais 2-0 on Sunday, November 8, in the 10th round. It was Lyon's first match since Paulo Fonseca's departure.

t: Ukraine: Russians, Ukrainians and Americans meet in Abu Dhabi
s: Russian, Ukrainian and US delegations opened a new round of US-brokered peace talks in Abu Dhabi on Tuesday, November 10, with the United States represented by Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner. According to The Washington Post, European security is on the agenda, after Jared Kushner proposed a new security architecture involving Russia and European countries.

t: Education: teachers, pupils and students strike again
s: The joint union front for state schools and higher education, joined by high-school and student organisations, called a new day of strikes and demonstrations on Tuesday, November 10, following one on November 5. It is demanding more resources for schools and universities; a further day of action has been announced for November 17.

t: CAC 40 gains 0.55% as oil prices fall
s: The Paris stock exchange closed up 0.55% at 8,278.59 points on Tuesday, November 10, supported by lower oil prices. The index did, however, pare its gains after the release of US inflation figures for October.

t: Nexperia swamped as AI soaks up chipmaking capacity
s: Dutch semiconductor maker Nexperia is "totally oversubscribed", its interim CEO told Reuters on Tuesday at the Electronica trade fair in Munich. Suppliers are shifting capacity towards AI data centres, at the expense of the mature chips used in cars and industrial equipment.

t: Google adds two AI chips to its eighth-generation TPU line
s: Google unveiled two new versions of its in-house AI chips on Tuesday, November 10, the TPU 8tx and the TPU 8i Max, adding to the eighth generation launched in April. The TPU 8i Max combines two TPU 8i chips in a single package.

t: Women's Champions League: PSG beaten 1-2 by Bayern
s: PSG lost 1-2 to Bayern Munich at the Parc des Princes on Tuesday, November 10, on matchday four of the league phase. Trailing 2-0 at half-time, the Paris side pulled one back through a Paulina Dudek penalty.

t: Women's Champions League: Paris FC outclassed in Madrid (3-0)
s: Paris FC lost 3-0 away to Real Madrid on Tuesday, November 10, on matchday four of the league phase. After a goalless first half, the Madrid side scored three times after the break.

t: Ukraine: Moscow and Kyiv agree on a large prisoner exchange
s: Three-way talks with the United States ended in Abu Dhabi on Wednesday 11 November. Russia and Ukraine agreed on a major exchange of prisoners of war, with no exact figure yet. US envoy Jared Kushner hailed a humanitarian breakthrough, but no progress was announced towards a peace deal.

t: Emmanuel Macron leads his last Armistice Day ceremony
s: On Wednesday 11 November, Emmanuel Macron led the ceremony for the 108th anniversary of the 1918 Armistice in Paris, for the last time as head of state. He laid a wreath at the statue of Clemenceau, then rekindled the flame of the Unknown Soldier under the Arc de Triomphe. In his speech, he said the memory of 11 November belongs in every school, amid a debate among teachers.

t: The CAC 40 gains 0.66% in a public-holiday session
s: On Wednesday 11 November, the CAC 40 rose 0.66% to 8,332.87 points, up 54.28 points on the previous day. Volumes were thin in Paris, with 11 November a public holiday.

t: COP31: Guterres calls for a climate justice pact
s: Addressing leaders gathered in Antalya for COP31, UN Secretary-General António Guterres proposed a "climate justice compact". It aims to help developing countries move away from fossil fuels and protect those already suffering from climate change. He also suggested taxing fossil fuel companies to help the hardest-hit countries.

t: Global fossil CO2 emissions set to fall in 2026
s: According to Global Carbon Budget 2026 data, global fossil CO2 emissions are expected to fall by 0.41% this year. The decline would come from oil (−1.89%), while coal-related emissions would rise (+0.57%). The fall does not necessarily mean that emissions have peaked.

t: Ukraine: Trump's envoys meet Putin, then head to Dublin
s: Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner met Vladimir Putin at the Kremlin on Thursday, November 12, for about two hours. The visit followed two days of talks between Russian, Ukrainian and US negotiators in Abu Dhabi that ended without a breakthrough. The envoys then travelled to Dublin to brief Volodymyr Zelensky.

t: Christophe Gleizes marks 500 days in detention in Algeria
s: French sports journalist Christophe Gleizes has spent 500 days in detention in Algeria, where he was sentenced to seven years in prison for "glorifying terrorism". His mother said "500 days is too much", and his supporters are calling for his release.

t: Nvidia shares plunge at the open after its CEO's exit
s: Nvidia shares fell about 13% at the open on Wall Street on Thursday, November 12, after the announcement of Jensen Huang's resignation.

t: Jensen Huang steps down at Nvidia, Colette Kress takes over on an interim basis
s: Nvidia's board accepted on Thursday, November 12, the resignation of co-founder and CEO Jensen Huang, effective immediately. Chief financial officer Colette Kress becomes interim CEO while keeping her role, until a successor is found. The departure follows revelations about Huang's private life that had led to an internal investigation.

t: COP31: cities take a seat at the leaders' summit
s: On Thursday, November 12, the COP31 leaders' summit in Antalya gave cities an unprecedented role, with a high-level dialogue on urban resilience and adaptation. Local leaders are pressing governments to turn their climate commitments into concrete action.

t: Nations League: beaten 3-1 by Italy, France lose for the first time under Zidane
s: France lost 3-1 to Italy on Thursday, November 12, at San Siro in Milan, on matchday 5 of the Nations League. It is the first defeat of the Zinédine Zidane era.

t: Ukraine: Europeans set to join next round of talks
s: US envoys say Russia and Ukraine have agreed to widen the next round of talks to include Europeans. The Kremlin has not confirmed this and says no concrete discussions on the matter have taken place. The Abu Dhabi round on November 10 and 11 was the first in nine months.

t: Guinea: ten dead in clashes over gold mining
s: Clashes between security forces and gold miners left ten dead, including five foreigners, and thirteen injured on Wednesday, November 11, near Siguiri, according to the government. Authorities banned what they call unregulated gold mining in the region in early November, and a judicial inquiry has been opened.

t: Gaza: nine-month-old baby dies of cold in Khan Younis
s: A nine-month-old baby died of hypothermia in his family's tent in Khan Younis, according to AFP as cited by Al Jazeera. More than 50 countries are calling on Israel to let in shelter, fuel and medical care.

t: Civil servants: Lecornu opens a month of talks, CFDT joins the strike
s: On Friday, November 13, Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu opened a month of talks with civil service unions on five topics, including low pay. He is due to meet them again on December 11. Judging the proposals insufficient, the unions are keeping their November 17 strike, which the CFDT union is now joining.

t: CAC 40 ends flat, posting a third weekly gain
s: The Paris stock exchange closed up 0.09% on Friday at 8,369 points, torn between good news from the United States and rising oil prices. Over the week, the CAC 40 gained 2.8%.

t: US producer prices slow in October
s: US producer prices rose 0.3% in October, less than the 0.4% expected, according to figures released on Friday. Year on year, they are up 6.5%, more than triple the Federal Reserve's target.

t: Brain implants: Synchron pauses its clinical trials
s: US start-up Synchron has paused enrolment in trials of its second-generation brain implant, after a performance problem with the lead connecting the electrode to the implanted electronics. The company says it is not a safety issue.

t: A new map of the brain's basal ganglia
s: A large research consortium has published a cell-by-cell map of the basal ganglia, a brain region involved in many diseases. The work reveals a previously unknown type of neuron linked to schizophrenia risk.

t: COP31: $10 billion targeted, far short of needs
s: At COP31 in Antalya, British, Norwegian and Canadian development finance institutions aim to mobilise $10 billion for climate projects in emerging markets by 2030. António Guterres called for reform of a financial system that he says is failing vulnerable countries.

t: COP31: Gavin Newsom announces $81 million for agriculture
s: California's governor spoke at the UN climate summit, saying America's climate fight is "far from over". He announced $81 million for climate-smart agriculture.

t: Rugby: France topple South Africa 21-19
s: France beat the Springboks 21-19 on Friday, November 13, at the Stade de France, in round 5 of the Nations Championship. They scored three tries before half-time, then held off a comeback from the two-time world champions.

t: Trump, Xi and Putin to hold three-way meeting in Shenzhen on Thursday
s: The White House announced on Saturday 14 November a first trilateral meeting between Donald Trump, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin, on Thursday 19 November, on the sidelines of the APEC summit in Shenzhen. According to US officials, nuclear weapons and the war in Iran will be discussed, but probably not Ukraine.

t: Ukraine: Washington raises NATO membership in exchange for Donbas withdrawal
s: Volodymyr Zelensky said US negotiators had asked whether Ukraine would withdraw its troops from Donbas in exchange for NATO membership. The Ukrainian president says he refuses any withdrawal. The Abu Dhabi talks, on 10 and 11 November, ended without a breakthrough.

t: Ukraine: at least 7 killed and 80 injured in Russian attacks
s: Russian attacks killed at least seven civilians and injured 80 in one day, according to regional authorities cited on Saturday 14 November. The Zaporizhzhia region was the hardest hit, with three dead, including a child, and 62 injured.

t: United States: thousands of flights cancelled after FAA outage
s: US air traffic remained heavily disrupted on Saturday 14 November, the day after a nationwide ground stop ordered by the FAA, the aviation authority. Nearly 6,500 flights were cancelled on Saturday and more than 8,000 delayed, according to FlightAware. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy pointed to work by a contractor on a telecommunications system managed by L3Harris.

t: In Peru, Pope Leo XIV calls for an end to violence
s: Visiting a remote town in the Peruvian Andes on Saturday 14 November, Pope Leo XIV called for an end to the violence gripping the country and urged people not to respond to injustice with brutality. Peru is the final leg of his South American trip.

t: Cost of living: 106,000 protesters on fifth Saturday of demonstrations
s: The interior ministry counted around 106,000 protesters on Saturday 14 November, including 24,000 in Paris; organisers claim 200,000. Yellow Vests, students and education unions marched over the cost of living, for school funding and against a police bill.

t: Wall Street: S&P 500 and Nasdaq fall, dragged down by Nvidia
s: On Friday 13 November, the S&P 500 lost 0.40% to 7,561.67 points and the Nasdaq 0.91% to 25,136.27 points, while the Dow Jones gained 0.10% to 52,347.55 points. Uncertainty over Nvidia weighed on technology stocks. Over the week, all three indexes rose by more than 2%.

t: AI: start-up LangChain valued at $3 billion
s: LangChain, which makes tools for managing artificial intelligence agents, has raised $300 million in a Series C round led by CapitalG, TechCrunch reported on Friday 13 November. The deal values the company at $3 billion.

t: SpaceX catches Starship's upper stage for the first time
s: On Saturday 14 November, the upper stage of the Starship rocket returned from orbit and was caught by the mechanical arms of its launch tower at Starbase, Texas. It is a first. The catch of the first stage, however, had been called off after lift-off.

t: Sleep: the brain's "rinse cycle" weakens with age
s: A study published on Friday 13 November in Nature Aging shows that the waves of cerebrospinal fluid that flow through the brain during deep sleep are reduced in older adults. The authors link this decline to the loss of the brain's slow waves and to vascular changes.

t: COP31: thousands march as negotiations make slow progress
s: Thousands of campaigners marched in Antalya on Saturday 14 November to demand finance and a just transition. The talks are making little progress: the final decision text remains a list of proposals, and a first draft is expected early in the week, as ministers arrive.

t: Rugby: Wales beat the All Blacks for the first time in 73 years
s: Wales beat New Zealand 35-28 on Saturday 14 November in Cardiff, in the Nations Championship. The Welsh had not won against the All Blacks for 73 years.

t: Coupe de France: Guingamp knocked out on penalties by Lannion
s: En Avant Guingamp, a Ligue 2 club, were knocked out on their first appearance in the seventh round of the Coupe de France (French Cup) on Saturday 14 November. After a 0-0 draw, Lannion, a fourth-tier National 2 club, won on penalties.

t: Hormuz: Iran says it downed a US drone, two tankers on fire
s: On Saturday 14 November, Iran's Revolutionary Guards said they had shot down a US MQ-1 drone over Qeshm Island, the 17th by their count. The Iranian navy also said two oil tankers had caught fire in the Strait of Hormuz after hitting mines. These statements come from the Iranian side alone.

t: Cape Verde: President Neves set for first-round re-election
s: Incumbent President José Maria Neves has nearly 64% of the vote in the presidential election held on Sunday 15 November, according to provisional results covering almost all polling stations. His main rival, former Justice Minister Joana Rosa, has 31.6%.

t: Cost of living: 404 arrests on the sidelines of Saturday's protests
s: The Interior Ministry announced on Sunday that 404 people were arrested in France on the sidelines of the protests on Saturday 14 November, including 126 in Paris. Ten police officers were slightly injured. In Paris, 108 people were taken into custody, 38 of them minors, according to the police prefecture.

t: Markets: Anthropic due on Nasdaq Thursday, Nvidia reports earnings
s: Artificial intelligence company Anthropic is due to price its initial public offering on Wednesday 18 November, with trading to begin on Thursday 19 on the Nasdaq under the ticker "ANT". Nvidia also reports its quarterly earnings this week.

t: Oil: Brent slips to around 95 dollars
s: On Monday morning in Asia, Brent for January delivery was down 0.9% at 95.00 dollars a barrel. Markets expect a return to a supply surplus in the fourth quarter, while keeping an eye on tensions in the Middle East.

t: AI: protesters in San Francisco call for a US-China treaty
s: Activists from the "Stop the AI Race" movement gathered outside OpenAI's headquarters in San Francisco. They are calling for a treaty between the United States and China to slow the development of artificial intelligence.

t: COP31: fossil fuel exit coalition presses on without Colombia
s: The coalition of states launched in April in Santa Marta to move away from fossil fuels is continuing its work at COP31 despite the withdrawal of Colombia, its founding country, confirmed by Ireland's climate department. It is due to publish a progress report this week on the steps taken by its members.

t: South-east France: orange alert lifted after heavy rain
s: The orange rain and flood alert was lifted on Sunday 15 November at 4 a.m. in the Hérault and Gard departments, then at 6 a.m. in Bouches-du-Rhône. Heavy rain fell overnight around Montpellier.

t: Football: France beat Turkey and reach the quarter-finals
s: France won 2-1 against Turkey on Sunday 15 November in Bordeaux, on the final matchday of the Nations League group stage. Turkey pulled a goal back late on through Bardakci. France qualify for the quarter-finals.

t: Rugby: England crush Japan 78-15, five tries for Joseph
s: England beat Japan 78-15 on Saturday 14 November at Twickenham in the Nations Championship. England scored thirteen tries, five of them by winger Will Joseph, who equals the national record for a single match.

t: Rugby: Ireland beat Fiji 43-15 ahead of South Africa
s: Ireland won 43-15 against Fiji on Saturday 14 November in Dublin in the Nations Championship. Ireland scored 26 unanswered points in the second half. They face South Africa next Saturday.

t: Tennis: Zverev opens his ATP Finals with a win over Jodar
s: Alexander Zverev beat Rafael Jodar 6-4, 6-4 on Sunday 15 November in Turin in his first round-robin match at the ATP Finals.

t: Ukraine: Moscow says it intercepted a record 1,336 drones
s: Russia's Defence Ministry says it intercepted 1,336 Ukrainian drones overnight from 15 to 16 November, over fifteen regions, occupied Crimea and two seas. According to Moscow's mayor, about 600 drones were heading for the capital's region and 191 were intercepted on their approach. Kyiv has not commented and the figures could not be independently verified.

t: Migration: five EU countries announce a deportation centre in Rwanda
s: Five European Union countries, including Germany and Denmark, on Monday 16 November unveiled a deal to set up a centre in Rwanda for deported migrants. It would be the first facility of its kind outside the bloc.

t: Gulf: Iran says it targeted a US radar in Bahrain
s: Iran's Revolutionary Guards say they launched six drones on Sunday 15 November at a US air defence radar at Riffa Air Base in Bahrain. Bahrain says its air defences intercepted the projectiles.

t: Francophonie: election of the secretary-general postponed
s: Meeting at a summit in Phnom Penh, the leaders of the Organisation internationale de la Francophonie (OIF, the body of French-speaking countries) on Monday 16 November postponed the election of their secretary-general. Emmanuel Macron welcomed a "compromise".

t: Civil service: a day of strikes and demonstrations this Tuesday
s: A day of action is planned this Tuesday 17 November, with strikes in the civil service and marches in several cities. On transport, a few Transilien suburban lines around Paris could be disrupted; traffic should be normal on TGV high-speed trains and RER lines, according to franceinfo.

t: Presidential race: five candidates debate poverty
s: Gabriel Attal, Raphaël Glucksmann, Marine Le Pen, Jean-Luc Mélenchon and Bruno Retailleau debated on Monday 16 November on the news channel LCI, in a programme organised with the food charity Restos du Cœur. Housing, charities and young people were at the centre of the exchanges.

t: Gérard Depardieu drops his appeal trial and apologises
s: The actor has dropped his appeal trial for sexual assault, which was due to open on Monday 16 November in Paris, and offered his apologies in a statement.

t: Wall Street slides ahead of Nvidia's results
s: On Monday 16 November, the S&P 500 lost 1.9%, the Nasdaq 2.5% and the Dow Jones 1.4%, or 739 points. Nvidia shares fell 4.1%, their third straight decline since Jensen Huang resigned as chief executive. The group reports its quarterly results this Tuesday after the close.

t: Paris stock market: the CAC 40 ends its winning streak
s: After five straight sessions of gains, the CAC 40 slipped 0.2% on Monday 16 November and closed at 8,352 points.

t: AI: Alibaba launches its new flagship model, Qwen4-Max
s: Chinese group Alibaba has unveiled Qwen4-Max, its new flagship artificial intelligence model. According to the company, it cuts the cost per task by about 60% and tightens its cybersecurity guardrails.

t: Fed: a governor warns of bank runs accelerated by AI
s: Michael Barr, a governor of the US Federal Reserve, warned on Monday 16 November that autonomous AI agents could speed up mass deposit withdrawals, to the point of bank runs unfolding in minutes.

t: Health: Apple launches a study on the use of AI for medical questions
s: Apple has launched a research study in the United States, run with the company OpenEvidence, on how the public uses conversational AI for health. It is open to up to 200,000 participants aged 21 and over.

t: COP31: a first draft deal signals tough negotiations
s: A first draft deal was published on Monday 16 November at COP31 in Antalya, Turkey. According to Australia's Chris Bowen, who is leading the negotiations, it contains clauses already rejected by some countries; it also offers two sets of wording on fossil fuels. The conference is due to end on 20 November.

t: COP31: AI holds "immense potential" and "great peril" for the climate
s: At COP31 in Antalya, the UN's climate chief, Simon Stiell, said artificial intelligence holds both "immense potential" and "great peril" for the climate.

t: Football: England end Spain's unbeaten run
s: England beat Spain 3-2 on Sunday 15 November in Madrid, in the Nations League. Spain had gone 43 matches without defeat.

t: Rugby: France climb back onto the world podium
s: After their win over South Africa, France climb to third place in the world rankings published on Monday 16 November.

t: Tennis: Alcaraz makes quick work of his ATP Finals opener in Turin
s: Carlos Alcaraz beat American Frances Tiafoe 6-2, 6-2 on Monday 16 November in his first match at the ATP Finals in Turin.

t: Tennis: Mirra Andreeva wins the WTA Finals without dropping a set
s: Russia's Mirra Andreeva beat Ukraine's Elina Svitolina 7-5, 6-3 on Sunday 15 November in the final of the WTA Finals. She did not drop a single set in the tournament.

t: Ukraine: Crimean Bridge hit again as Kyiv's bridges are targeted
s: Ukraine struck the bridge linking Russia to Crimea on Tuesday, November 17, for the second day running; according to Ukraine's General Staff, part of the road section collapsed. Overnight, Russia targeted Kyiv's northern and southern bridges over the Dnipro, which were closed to traffic.

t: APEC: leaders arrive in Shenzhen for the summit
s: Leaders of the APEC economies are arriving in Shenzhen, in southern China, for the November 18-19 summit. A three-way meeting between Donald Trump, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin is planned on the sidelines, a first.

t: Public sector: a smaller turnout in the fight over pay
s: On Tuesday, November 17, 146,000 people marched across France according to the Interior Ministry, and more than 500,000 according to the CGT union. Public-sector unions are demanding pay rises.

t: Drug trafficking: life sentences for the killers of Amine Kessaci's brother
s: The Aix-en-Provence assize court on Monday, November 16, sentenced two leading figures of Marseille's drug underworld to life imprisonment for a triple murder committed in 2020. One of the victims was the brother of anti-drug activist Amine Kessaci.

t: Paris stocks: CAC 40 falls 1.62%, dragged down by luxury
s: The CAC 40 closed sharply lower on Tuesday, November 17, at 8,216.78 points. Luxury stocks weighed, with Hermès losing more than 5%, amid nervousness ahead of Nvidia's results.

t: Wall Street: the Dow Jones loses more than 800 points
s: The Dow Jones fell 848.75 points (−1.64%) on Tuesday and the S&P 500 1.03%, to its lowest close since July. Nvidia's slide ahead of its results dragged tech stocks down.

t: Nvidia beats expectations in its first results without Jensen Huang
s: Nvidia reported quarterly revenue of $115.8 billion on Tuesday, November 17, against $109.1 billion expected, and forecasts about $130 billion for the current quarter. These are the first results presented by Colette Kress, interim chief executive since Jensen Huang's departure.

t: Proton brings its Lumo AI assistant to the desktop
s: Swiss company Proton on Tuesday launched a desktop version of Lumo, its privacy-focused AI assistant, for Windows, macOS and Linux.

t: COP31: the draft final deal stokes tensions
s: The first draft of COP31's final decision, in Antalya, is dividing delegations. Australian minister Chris Bowen, who is steering the negotiations, acknowledged the text contains elements that not all parties agree on; the conference is due to end on Friday, November 20.

t: COP31: Arab Group and Russia reject the text, EU backs electrification
s: The Arab Group and Russia rejected the draft final decision over its passages on fossil fuels and an electrification goal. The European Union, by contrast, backed that goal.

t: Climate: Dominica, Myanmar and Honduras hit hardest over 30 years
s: A new ranking presented at COP31 puts Dominica, Myanmar and Honduras at the top of the countries hardest hit by extreme weather over thirty years. The conference devoted Tuesday to the oceans.

t: Nations League: Haaland sends Norway through deep into stoppage time
s: Trailing 2-0 in Denmark, Norway won 3-2 on Tuesday, November 17, thanks to an Erling Haaland penalty in stoppage time. They take the last quarter-final spot.

t: Tennis: Arthur Fils claims his first win at the ATP Finals in Turin
s: Arthur Fils beat Spain's Rafael Jodar, who was hampered physically, 4-6, 6-2, 6-2 on Tuesday, November 17. The Frenchman stays in the race for the semi-finals ahead of facing Alexander Zverev on Thursday.

t: Gulf: Iran targets a US base in Kuwait and sites in Bahrain
s: On Wednesday 18 November, Iran targeted the Ali Al-Salem air base in Kuwait and several sites in Bahrain, in retaliation for a US strike the day before on a missile launch site on Qeshm Island. Kuwait's military said it intercepted drones. Qatar, a mediator, condemned a "dangerous escalation".

t: APEC: Xi Jinping welcomes Donald Trump in Shenzhen
s: Donald Trump arrived in Shenzhen on Wednesday for the APEC summit and was greeted by Xi Jinping at the foot of Air Force One. An unprecedented three-way meeting with Vladimir Putin is scheduled for Thursday, on the sidelines of the summit.

t: Budget: Lecornu to list his priorities for a compromise
s: Public accounts minister David Amiel told the Senate on Wednesday that Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu would present the priority topics for budget talks "in the coming days". The government is seeking a compromise with the mainstream right and left, as the Senate is due to start examining the bill on Friday.

t: Paris stock market: CAC 40 falls 0.85% despite Nvidia
s: The CAC 40 closed down 0.85% on Wednesday at 8,146.83 points, a day after a 1.62% drop. Nvidia's strong results were not enough to reassure investors, who stayed cautious ahead of the US Federal Reserve's meeting minutes. Soitec and STMicroelectronics were among the biggest gainers.

t: Microsoft: Nadella explains the buyout offered to 60,000 employees
s: At the DealBook summit in New York on Wednesday, Microsoft chief Satya Nadella explained the voluntary buyout offered in October to 60,000 employees. He said it aims to reorganise work around AI rather than simply replace staff.

t: Google adds temporary conversations to its AI Mode
s: Google is adding "temporary threads" to the AI Mode of its search engine. These conversations are not saved to search history and are not used to personalise recommendations.

t: Migraine and smoking: a higher risk of early stroke
s: A study published on 18 November in the journal Neurology, based on Danish registry data on nearly 1.7 million women who had given birth, shows that the combination of migraine and smoking is associated with the highest risk of early stroke and death.

t: COP31: ministers try to unblock the negotiations
s: On the tenth day of COP31 in Antalya, disagreements between delegations remain numerous. Ministers are trying to bring positions closer before the scheduled close on Friday, notably on phasing out fossil fuels, adaptation finance and the timetable for the next IPCC reports. A new draft decision is expected on Thursday morning.

t: COP31: global electrification, a flagship but uncertain goal
s: The Turkish COP31 presidency is championing a goal for electricity to account for 35% of global energy consumption by 2035. It says 75 countries and 94 organisations back it, including France, through ecological transition minister Monique Barbut. Whether it makes it into the final agreement remains uncertain.

t: In Shenzhen, Trump, Xi and Putin sign a "peace declaration"
s: Meeting in China on Thursday, November 19 for an unprecedented three-way summit, the American, Chinese and Russian leaders issued a short declaration stating that a nuclear war cannot be won. The text provides for no talks on a nuclear arms reduction treaty, and no agreement was reached on Ukraine or Iran. Vladimir Putin said Ukraine and Europe were not ready to make compromises.

t: Four departments on orange alert for rain and flooding
s: On Thursday, November 19, the Landes, Seine-Maritime, Somme and Pas-de-Calais departments were placed on orange alert for rain and flooding by the national weather service, Météo-France. Pas-de-Calais was also on orange alert for river flooding.

t: Paris stocks fall, overshadowed by Anthropic's debut
s: The CAC 40 lost 0.81% on Thursday, November 19, to 8,080.74 points. Investors were focused on Anthropic's stock market listing in New York, against a backdrop of still-high interest rates.

t: Anthropic gains 17% in its first Nasdaq session
s: Priced at $83, Anthropic shares (ticker ANT) opened on Thursday, November 19 at $111.50 before paring their gains to close at $97.17. The session was volatile, in a falling tech market.

t: Palo Alto Networks buys AI start-up Applied Compute
s: The US cybersecurity company announced a deal to acquire Applied Compute, a privately held firm specialising in training and running AI models, for $4.5 billion paid in shares. Completion is expected in the third quarter of its 2027 fiscal year, subject to regulatory clearance.

t: COP31: final hours of talks for an uncertain deal
s: In Antalya, Turkey, nearly 200 countries are trying to wrap up the UN climate conference, due to end on Friday, November 20. According to AFP, the new draft decision published on Thursday no longer mentions oil, gas or coal.

t: Cost of living: unions in seven European countries call for protests
s: Unions and associations in seven European countries are calling for coordinated protests against the rising cost of living, from Friday, November 20 to Sunday, November 22. Their demands include measures on housing, prices and wages.

t: 2027 presidential race: Dominique de Villepin officially a candidate
s: The former prime minister made his candidacy for the 2027 presidential election official on Friday, November 20, at a press conference in Paris. He presents himself as an alternative to the far-right Rassemblement national, the hard-left La France insoumise and President Macron's camp. Polling at around 3% of voting intentions, he still has to gather the required sponsorships from elected officials.

t: Public sector: new strike call for December 1
s: The public-sector union coalition is calling for a new day of strikes and protests on Tuesday, December 1, the fourth since the start of the autumn. The unions are demanding that the "point d'indice", the base used to calculate civil servants' pay, be unfrozen. They are also inviting private-sector workers to march alongside public-sector staff.

t: Bank overdrafts: new rules come into force
s: New rules on authorised overdrafts, part of the reform of consumer credit, have applied since Friday, November 20. Overdrafts granted before that date are not affected.

t: Paris stock market: the CAC 40 loses 5.27% over the week
s: The CAC 40 fell for a fifth straight session on Friday, November 20 and ended the week below 8,000 points. Over five days, the Paris index lost 5.27%, amid distrust of stocks linked to artificial intelligence.

t: European Commission confirms an AI-assisted cyberattack
s: The European Commission confirmed on Thursday, November 19 that artificial intelligence tools were used in a cyberattack detected on October 22. Internal staff systems, including payroll and medical-expense reimbursement, were disrupted. The Commission did not say who was behind the attack.

t: COP31: no deal as negotiations go into overtime
s: The UN climate conference in Antalya, Turkey, was due to end on Friday, November 20, but no agreement had been reached by the evening. COP31's Turkish president, Murat Kurum, announced a new compromise proposal for Saturday. The European Union considers the current draft "not acceptable".

t: COP31: France and Panama demand a reference to fossil fuels
s: A group of countries from Europe, Africa, Latin America and the Pacific, led by France and Panama, is challenging the draft deal, which no longer explicitly mentions moving away from fossil fuels. Panama is threatening to object to any text that leaves it out. Since decisions are taken by consensus, a single objection can block the agreement.

t: Ligue 1: Troyes beat Le Havre 3-1
s: Troyes beat Le Havre 3-1 on Friday, November 20 at the Stade de l'Aube, in the 11th round of Ligue 1. It was a good result for Troyes in their fight to stay up, while Le Havre, playing their first match under coach Valérien Ismaël, are still struggling.

t: Ukraine: Russian attack kills a child and a paramedic in Kryvyi Rih
s: A Russian attack hit Kryvyi Rih, Volodymyr Zelensky's home city, on Saturday 21 November. Missiles struck near a restaurant, then drones targeted rescuers. A 7-year-old boy and a 20-year-old paramedic were killed, and more than 50 people were injured.

t: Presidential race: François Ruffin withdraws his bid
s: The Somme MP announced on Saturday 21 November that he will not run in 2027. He said he was acknowledging the "impasse" of his campaign, in the absence of a broad left-wing primary. He has not endorsed any other candidate.

t: Dominique de Villepin officially runs for president
s: The former prime minister announced his bid for the 2027 presidential election at a press conference in Paris on Friday 20 November. He called Macronism a "zombie power". He founded the La France humaniste movement in 2025.

t: CAC 40 loses 5.27% in a week and falls back below 8,000
s: The Paris stock exchange posted five straight losing sessions through Friday 20 November. The CAC 40 shed 5.27% over the week and closed below the 8,000-point mark. Distrust of AI stocks spreading from Wall Street weighed on markets.

t: Wall Street: S&P 500 and Dow enter correction territory
s: On Friday 20 November, the S&P 500 and the Dow closed more than 10% below their records, the threshold for a correction. The Nasdaq wiped out its 2026 gains. A massive sell-off in artificial intelligence stocks drove most of the decline.

t: Nvidia plunges after reports of an accounting review
s: According to Reuters, staff at the SEC, the US market regulator, are examining possible accounting issues at Nvidia. The stock fell at least 10% on Friday 20 November and had its worst week since 2008. The company has been in turmoil since the resignation of its founder Jensen Huang.

t: COP31: Turkish presidency says final deal is close
s: The Antalya talks overran their scheduled Friday close. COP31 President Murat Kurum presented overnight a text he considers acceptable to all parties, with a view to adopting it on Sunday. The draft has been criticised for not explicitly mentioning a move away from fossil fuels.

t: Rugby: France crush Argentina to reach the final
s: Les Bleus beat Argentina 45-17 at the Stade de France on Saturday 21 November, scoring seven tries. Trailing 10-7 in the first half, they dominated the second. They will play South Africa in the Nations Championship final.

t: Ligue 1: PSG come back to beat Nice 3-2 and extend lead
s: PSG won 3-2 in Nice on Saturday 21 November, on matchday 11, after trailing. Substitute Ferran Torres scored the late winner. Paris have now won eight league games in a row and lead by five points, having played one game more.
